record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
record.original_question: How can the organization of interacting-shell-model eigenfunctions near a particle-emission threshold be made quantitatively predictive, especially for the ground state of 11Li where low-lying two-neutron and one-neutron emission thresholds are separated by less than 30 keV and may determine the relative weights of configurations associated with the two-neutron continuum of 9Li and with unbound 10Li channels?

evidence.quote: We are still far away from a quantitative understanding of the organization of ISM eigenfunctions near the particle emission threshold.

The structure of the ground state wave function of 11Li is a particularly interesting case-study due to an intricate sequence of low-lying two- and one-neutron emission thresholds which are separated by less than 30 keV (!).
This approximate degeneracy of two different emission thresholds may have important consequences on the structure of halo two-neutron pair.

The relative weights of configurations, such as [9Li(3/2−)]⊗[n2(0+)], corresponding to the two-neutron continuum of 9Li, and {[9Li(1/2−)]⊗[n(1/2−)]}1+⊗[n(1/2−)], {[9Li(1/2−)]⊗[n(1/2+)]}1−⊗[n(1/2+)], or {[9Li(3/2−)]⊗[n(1/2−)]}2+⊗[n(1/2−)], associated with an unbound 10Li, reflects the influence of these two almost degenerate branch points on the structure of the ground state wave function of 11Li.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an interacting shell-model (ISM) description of a finite nuclear many-body system in which single-particle states are organized into bound, resonant, and scattering components, and the eigenfunctions of the effective Hamiltonian are expanded in a configuration basis that includes both bound configurations and configurations coupled to particle-emission continua. Suppose the system has several particle-emission channels whose thresholds (branch points of the resolvent in the complex energy plane) lie close to one another, so that the ground state is energetically very near these thresholds.

Develop a quantitatively predictive framework that determines how ISM eigenfunctions reorganize as a function of the proximity to particle-emission thresholds, and apply it to the following concrete situation: a three-body-like halo system consisting of a core C with low-lying states C(3/2^-) and C(1/2^-), plus two valence neutrons, in which the one-neutron emission threshold (to an unbound C+n subsystem with channels {[C(1/2^-)] ⊗ [n(1/2^-)]}_{1^+}, {[C(1/2^-)] ⊗ [n(1/2^+)]}_{1^-}, and {[C(3/2^-)] ⊗ [n(1/2^-)]}_{2^+}) and the two-neutron emission threshold (to C(3/2^-) plus a correlated [n^2(0^+)] pair in the two-neutron continuum) are separated by less than 30 keV.

Problem: Derive, from the underlying continuum-coupled shell-model Hamiltonian, quantitative expressions for the relative spectroscopic weights of the configurations
  (i)  [C(3/2^-)] ⊗ [n^2(0^+)],
  (ii) {[C(1/2^-)] ⊗ [n(1/2^-)]}_{1^+} ⊗ [n(1/2^-)],
  (iii){[C(1/2^-)] ⊗ [n(1/2^+)]}_{1^-} ⊗ [n(1/2^+)],
  (iv) {[C(3/2^-)] ⊗ [n(1/2^-)]}_{2^+} ⊗ [n(1/2^-)],
in the ground-state wave function of the three-body halo, as functions of the (small) energy gap Δ between the one- and two-neutron branch points, and prove a quantitative criterion describing how the near-degeneracy of these two branch points controls the configuration mixing in the limit Δ → 0.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of a quantitative theory for ISM eigenfunction organization near particle-emission thresholds, including the configuration structure of the 11Li ground state with its near-degenerate one- and two-neutron thresholds, remains an active research topic in nuclear open quantum systems. Continuum shell model and Gamow shell model studies (Michel, Nazarewicz, Płoszajczak and collaborators, 2010s–2020s) have made progress on threshold effects (e.g., near-threshold clustering, continuum coupling), but no fully predictive quantitative theory specific to the 11Li sub-30-keV threshold separation has been established.

status_evidence.snippet: We are still far away from a quantitative understanding of the organization of ISM eigenfunctions near the particle emission threshold.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as open in the source listing of open problems.

status_evidence.title: Gamow shell model description of weakly bound and unbound nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Recent reviews of Gamow/continuum shell model approaches discuss threshold effects but do not provide a closed quantitative theory for 11Li-type near-degenerate thresholds.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature treats the problem as still under active development.
